1.1 D- and L- Relative Configuration Conventions (Spatial Arrangement of Highest-Numbered Chiral Carbon C-5)

D/L Stereochemistry vs Optical Rotation (+ Dextro / - Levo): D-(+)-Glucose vs D-(-)-Fructose
quickSummary: Carbohydrates are polyhydroxy aldehydes or ketones. Relative D/L configuration is assigned by comparing the highest-numbered asymmetric carbon (C-5 in aldohexoses) with D-glyceraldehyde (OH on right = D; OH on left = L). D/L designation has no direct relationship to the sign of optical rotation (+/-).
summary: Master carbohydrate taxonomy, Fischer D/L stereochemical conventions, and optical rotation distinction.

conceptBreakdown.content:
Relative configuration is assigned by comparing the spatial arrangement of the asymmetric carbon furthest from the carbonyl group (the highest-numbered chiral carbon, e.g., C-5 in aldohexoses) with D-Glyceraldehyde:
- **D-Configuration**: The hydroxyl (-OH) group at the highest-numbered chiral center lies on the RIGHT side in Fischer projection.
- **L-Configuration**: The hydroxyl (-OH) group at the highest-numbered chiral center lies on the LEFT side in Fischer projection.
- **D/L vs. (+/-)**: Natural D-Glucose is dextrorotatory [D-(+)-glucose]; natural D-Fructose is levorotatory [D-(-)-fructose].

quickRevision: Monosaccharides: cannot be hydrolyzed further (Glucose, Fructose).
D-Configuration: C-5 -OH on the RIGHT in Fischer projection.
L-Configuration: C-5 -OH on the LEFT in Fischer projection.
D/L configuration is independent of optical rotation sign (+/-).
